sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0) WebGPURenderer; WebGPU with WebGL 2 fallback; Rapier 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio API; PeerJS 1.5.5; AI Hub Session Protocol v1, client 1.4.0; HTML/CSS/JavaScript
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded and ink-outlined 3D mansion, moonlit teal, warm amber matches and illustrated furnishings
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, AnimationClip and keyframe tracks for walking, breathing, ghosts, bat wings, spider legs and clocks; procedural secondary effects
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated Web Audio waltz at 10% music volume by default, 16 synthesized sound effects and Animalese-style gibberish voices; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub host-authoritative shared-world co-op for 1–4; standalone PeerJS/WebRTC co-op for 1–4 with same-origin BroadcastChannel transport; shared-screen local co-op for 1–2
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium 153 with Playwright 1.63; software WebGPU state checks; complete normal-physics and attract playthroughs; emulated standard gamepad, keyboard, mouse and touch; OfflineAudioContext; file:// launch; TV screenshots through WebGL fallback; official AI Hub harness; actual WebRTC with loopback enabled
sourceInformation.research: Atari official Haunted House source page (https://atari.com/pages/hauntedhouse); original instruction manual (https://static.atariage.com/manual_html_page.php?SoftwareLabelID=233); official AI Hub documentation and harness; Three.js r180 WebGPURenderer source; Rapier character-controller documentation. Researched urn, one-hand inventory, matches, four floors/six rooms, enemies, darkness and sound cues.

testingFeedback: Testing caught 2 game issues: furniture crowded a stair landing and delayed initialization could miss the four-player Hub handshake deadline. Both were fixed.
1 critical integration issue: the four-player Hub startup deadline could prevent a round from starting. The stair issue blocked the scripted route but could be approached from an adjacent point.
The complete four-floor playthrough through normal Rapier movement, pickups, locks, urn merging, stairs and escape was most helpful; it found the blocked landing.
Initial headless WebGPU screenshots were least helpful because they could be blank. Runtime state checks and WebGL diagnostic screenshots provided useful evidence.
engineFeedback: Three.js scene graphs and AnimationMixer made it straightforward to build expressive procedural characters, distinct rooms and reusable native animation clips.
Headless WebGPU framebuffer capture was unreliable. I also initially placed the Hub handshake after expensive initialization; the final game connects in the head before loading its modules.
The most important custom system was the shared game state: one-hand inventory, urn assembly, mansion navigation and authoritative co-op synchronization.
The hardest part was keeping Rapier colliders and navigation synchronized with changing floor decorations while supporting every input device.
none; no engine source was modified.
I would improve reliable WebGPU framebuffer capture in headless software browsers.
promptFeedback: The controller-first UX, attract mode, source research and concrete packaging requirements gave the project a clear and useful target.
Haunted House (1982) can refer to the Atari 2600 game or a Gottlieb pinball table. I used the Atari 2600 game.
The hardest requirement was completing the gameplay, four input styles, live developer tools and authoritative multiplayer together inside one shareable HTML file.
I would specify the source platform and put the mandatory feedback fields in one compact schema at the beginning.

aiHub.name: Haunted House Party
aiHub.tagline: The guests are dead. The evening is alive.
aiHub.description: Explore a moonlit, ink-outlined mansion by matchlight. Carry one object at a time, outwit spiders, bats and a wall-walking host, and reunite a broken urn before you lose your last nerve; bring friends for shared-house co-op.
aiHub.controls: WASD/left stick move; Space/Square light; E/Cross interact; Shift/Circle dodge; Q/Triangle drop; Tab/L1 journal; Esc/Options pause; touch drag, context tap and double-tap dodge.
